area_title: Encapsulating DbContext configuration and minimizing API surface
what_area_is_about: DbContext configuration details leaking into Program.cs via AddDbContext options-builder chains
sensitive-data logging and SQL parameter logging as examples of configuration details that should not be scattered through client code
passing only environment-dependent parameters such as connection string and logging flag
moving EF Core provider/logging setup into SchoolContext.OnConfiguring
reducing public API/configuration surface by using a small constructor or factory registration
preserving scoped DbContext lifetime with AddScoped while hiding option-builder complexity
key_ideas: Encapsulation applies to infrastructure code, not only domain models.
Startup/Program.cs should not need to know every internal EF Core configuration detail when the DbContext can own it.
Expose only parameters that vary by environment; hide stable composition logic inside the DbContext.
Sensitive-data logging is a useful example because its accidental exposure can leak query parameters into logs.
Manual AddScoped factory registration can preserve the same scoped lifetime while exposing a smaller application-facing surface.
Simple AddDbContext configuration can remain as-is; encapsulation becomes valuable when the options chain grows.
